## PATCH 3 (review revision) — UNCOMPILED / UNEXECUTED review material. Supersedes PATCH 2; PATCH 2 is preserved above as history.

Status of this revision: source and controls only, in a local commit on a session branch. **No compiler, test, claim, regen, run, dispatch, push or host contact has been performed by this session.** Nothing below is labelled RED or GREEN. `sleek-owl-397`'s and `keen-otter-392`'s findings on PATCH 2 are accepted as **source-review conclusions, not execution evidence**.

### 1. What changed since PATCH 2, item by item

**BLOCKING 1 — `reading_a_base_changes_the_report_line_and_not_the_published_payload` would have gone RED on correct code.** Confirmed from source: `reuse_tally` began from `population_parse_begin(classes: [], ...)`, so the three `JudgedRefused` rows in `every_declared_met` were undeclared refusals, `report.held` was false, and the `off.report.held == true` baseline did not exist; and the fold used `judge`, which takes the verdict shortcut and never consults the base. Fixed by (a) a new `reuse_tally_declared`, which begins from `fixture_classes` so the refusals the fold replays are the ones declared, and (b) a new `judge_read`, which walks the production sequence **standing -> counted -> accepted** for a parses row and standing->counted->refused for a refused row. The classes-free `reuse_tally` is retained only for the standing-rule controls, which assert one lookup and carry no refusals.

**MAJOR 2 — the payload-parity halves could not fail.** Confirmed: `population_parse_accepted` never reads `reuse`, so sending both halves through it made the pair unfalsifiable, and the real decision (`population_parse_member`: Reused -> accept, else `acquisition_parse`) never executed. The four controls that did that are **deleted**, not annotated, and replaced by six controls that drive the decision body itself:

| control | what it drives | mutation it would catch |
|---|---|---|
| `a_reused_member_is_accepted_without_the_parser_being_asked` | Reused arm, member whose text **cannot parse** | delete the Reused arm / fall through to the parser; or accept without counting |
| `a_base_under_another_identity_sends_the_unreused_member_to_the_parser` | unparsable member, its own line in the base under **another** parse-compiler identity | standing lookup ignoring the identity field |
| `a_base_without_the_digest_sends_the_member_to_the_parser` | unparsable member, right identity, digest the base never carried | standing lookup calling an unseen digest Reused |
| `a_refused_member_publishes_nothing_for_itself` | reuse off, unparsable member | recording a receipt for a refused member |
| `a_parsed_member_publishes_the_line_the_writer_will_publish` | parsable member, reuse off | publishing a line other than the schema writer's |
| `a_mixed_walk_publishes_its_own_lines_in_walk_order` | two parsable members, base covering only the first; warm/cold **and** warm-reversed/cold-reversed | publishing under another member's key; sorting the artifact; a "reuse" that never reused |

The first three are the discriminating ones: their members **cannot parse**, so an acceptance is reachable only along the Reused arm, and the two that must be refused are refused by the real parser, not asserted.

**The seam, and what it leaves open.** `population_parse_member`'s decision body is now `population_parse_member_decided(env, member, tally)`; the original function still performs the lookup and delegates, so behaviour is unchanged and every real walk runs the same body. The claim supplies the `(file, content)` pair the lookup would have returned — the boundary this claim answers for (DESIGN §3) — and nothing else: digest, standing, counting, the branch and `acquisition_parse` are production code, over the environment the production route builds (`module_acquisition.acquisition_env` over `repository_storage_layout()`; `bindings: []` because only the lookup reads them). **The real-producer inhabitance obligation remains OPEN**: no claim here executes the member lookup, the CLI, or the artifact save; those run in `gunbc test //gunbc/instruments:v2-native-cli`'s walked live-root controls (`src/v1/stage0/src/cli_run/native_lane_runner.rs`, `walk_population_controls`), which this session has not executed. The three obligations are listed at the foot of the claim file rather than assumed away.

**MINOR 4 — stale "read as complete" claims.** Removed from `compile_cli`'s `Absent` arm and from the `a_walk_with_no_compiler_offers_no_receipts_payload` comment. Both now say what is true: a base carrying no lines answers every member lookup with a **miss**, so an empty base grants no member anything — which is exactly why `population_verdict_products` does not claim to guard it.

**MINOR 5 — the writer's `Absent` arm.** It is unreachable from any accepted invocation (`needs_compiler` requires `--compiler` whenever `--receipts` or `--write-identity` is asked for, and `population_verdict_products` returns receipts exactly when a compiler is named). It is kept because the match must be total, is labelled **UNREACHABLE / UNTESTED**, and its scope is named as one hypothetical (a future `population_verdict_products` returning `Absent` while a compiler is named). The compiler-less control is now labelled **PRODUCER-ONLY** and cannot reach the writer at all. No partial-write semantics are claimed to be covered.

**MINOR 6 — "the purity oracle" and different-tree parity.** The phrase is gone from the control that claimed it; that control now states it is **not** the oracle, names the row that owns the phrase (`gunbc.recurring_failure_mode.cache_impurity`, "byte-identical cached-vs-cold is the purity oracle"), and restricts its own claim to holding the published payload fixed while the counts line moves. The note's §10 item 2 (a hit push compared with a closure-changing push) is **withdrawn**: same-tree, same-identity, one-cold-and-one-reusing is the only comparison that speaks to purity, and **no such pair has been executed**.

**MINOR 7 — the locator comment.** Reworded to state the mechanism instead of an ordinal metaphor: the locator emits `git rev-list --first-parent --skip=<ordinal> --max-count=1 <start>`, so ordinal N is the N-th ancestor **strictly below** the start and the start itself is reachable only at `--skip=0`, which no caller asks for. Behaviour unchanged.

### 3. Extraction and verification recipe (verified by the author reading this comment back)

```
# 1. recover the cumulative patch
sed -n '/^## PATCH 3/,$p' COMMENT.md | awk '/^```$/{n++; next} n==1' | base64 -d | gunzip > change1.patch
sha256sum change1.patch        # expect 8fbe9a2ce0ddedef4dcd42f9d17d7646fbad594a33dbeab91fe2b41ea2e81cab
wc -c change1.patch            # expect 69795

# 2. apply it to a clean base and check the TREE, not the commit sha
git checkout ed007978dc2a67096df619b1b91566458dfb2ffd
git apply change1.patch && git add -A && git write-tree
# expect 810baa3e8e7813135b00215ab369ca1ea1df8313

# 3. recover the raw commit object and check its identity
awk '/^## PATCH 3/{f=1} f' COMMENT.md | awk '/^```$/{n++; next} n==3' | base64 -d | gunzip > commit.txt
sha256sum commit.txt           # expect 010fcd99d249fc4814f934f8b107c9b4e103ea4eb4aa00de027ba01b1e69d5c7
git hash-object -t commit commit.txt
# expect ebea6caf22f0a3e4d075f666a558218e004be79e
```

### 4. What CI would and would not cover, if this were ever run

`src/v2/cli/compile_cli.dag` and `src/v2/cli/population_verbs.dag` are inside the emitted closure `v2.cli.compile_cli` (229 modules, static import closure), so the emit+build steps **would typecheck** the seam, the products split and the CLI rewiring — a missing symbol there is a real RED. `dag/gunbc/parse_verdict_restore.dag`, `dag/gunbc/parse_verdict_publish.dag` and **both** claim files are outside both emitted closures (`v2.cli.compile_cli`, `v2.compiler.source_root_eval`): nothing in CI typechecks them and no CI job runs v1 unit tests or witnesses, so a missing symbol in the new controls is **NO_OBSERVATION, never a RED**. Every new import was checked by static resolution against the target module's declarations (21/21 resolve), which is a text check, not a compile.
